transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump is poised to announce new updates to the America.gov website today.
NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports Trump will be joined by other administration officials and
AI industry leaders.
The White House has been featuring a countdown clock leading up to the announcement.
A White House official says the new website integrates artificial intelligence tools to
make it easier for Americans to access federal information and resources that are currently
spread out over several government agencies.
It's not yet clear exactly what resources the administration plans to feature on the
website.
Trump has taken an aggressive stance on AI and has been cozy with tech companies.
Industry leaders from tech companies, health and agriculture will be at the event, as well
as Vice President J.D. Dance.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, the White House.
The Trump administration banned about $1 billion in Canadian products overnight.
These include alcohol and dairy.
This is part of President Trump's trade war against Canada.
A bill designed to reform college athletics is heading to the House now that it has cleared
the Senate.
The Protect College Sports Act was approved by the Senate on a vote of 77 to 22, and bears
Becky Sullivan reports.
Supporters of the bill say it's needed to curtail chaos in college sports, where lawsuits
have chipped away at longstanding NCAA rules around amateurism, transfers and eligibility.
The legislation would give the NCAA a limited antitrust exemption in order to restore some
of those rules.
Critics felt it didn't go far enough to rein in other runaway spending on things like recruiting
and facilities and coaching salaries.
This was a bipartisan bill with bipartisan opposition.
Yays and nays came from Republicans and Democrats alike.
In a statement, NCAA President Charlie Baker thanked senators, but noted there's still
much work left to do.
The bill is supported by President Trump, but first it must pass the House, which has
gone on recess until after the midterms.
Becky Sullivan, NPR News.
Lindsey Clancy is due back in a Massachusetts courtroom today.
It will be for the first time since a mistrial was declared in her murder case.
Clancy had been charged with killing her three children.
At Member Station WBUR, Deborah Becker reports a hearing is being held to determine if Clancy
will be retried.
Clancy's defense has filed a flurry of motions, including one to dismiss the case.
The defense argues that the judge didn't have to declare a mistrial and should have investigated
reports that one of the 12 jurors wasn't following the law.
Retired Judge Jack Lew doesn't expect any quick decisions on the motions.
I would think the most likely scenario is people ask for time to address these issues.
Prosecutors have not said if they'll seek a new trial on first-degree murder charges
or try to negotiate a plea deal.
For NPR News, I'm Deborah Becker in Boston.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Former Special Counsel Jack Smith is scheduled to testify today before the Senate Judiciary
Committee.
Lawmakers are reviewing his probes of President Trump.
Some Republican lawmakers want to see Smith criminally prosecuted.
Smith says if he had the same set of facts presented to him today, he would again choose
to prosecute a president, regardless of party.
A federal judge is blocking President Trump's effort to withhold counterterrorism funding
to states if they don't go along with his election demands.
Earlier this year, FEMA told some jurisdictions they would not get certain grants unless they
released certain voter data.
The judge says Trump is exceeding his authority here.
A British chess prodigy has become the youngest player to earn the title "Woman Grandmaster,"
and she's only 11 years old.
NPR's Lauren Frayer has more from London.
Bodhana Sivanandhan uses a booster seat to reach the chessboard.
She's Britain's youngest women's chess champion and the youngest person overall to represent
England internationally in any sport.
On Sunday at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Uzbekistan, she clinched the highest title a female player
can attain, and she'll hold it for life.
She told reporters there, "I want to keep going and keep making history as well instead
of just stop here."
In addition to traveling the world to play chess tournaments, Bodhana is in the British
equivalent of sixth grade, and is on her way home now to catch up on school assignments.
Lauren Frayer, NPR News, London
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.

prices.

Drink responsibly.

Trump administration banned approximately $1 billion in Canadian products including alcohol and dairy
Senate approves Protect College Sports Act 77-22, bill heads to House for consideration
Lindsey Clancy returns to Massachusetts courtroom for hearing on whether case will be retried
Former Special Counsel Jack Smith scheduled to testify before Senate Judiciary Committee on Trump probes
Federal judge blocks Trump effort to withhold counterterrorism funding over election demands
British chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandhan becomes youngest Woman Grandmaster at age 11
